title: Sixth, Fifth, Third, Second — and Now First: Neumann Tops the Ladder
title_candidates: Sixth, Fifth, Third, Second — and Now First: Neumann Tops the Ladder
The Ladder and the Landslide: Neumann Climbs While Alex Baker Digs
Twenty-Seven Shots Apart: Estoril Writes Both Records in One Afternoon
From Two Spoons to the Trophy: Neumann Leads From the First Evening
theme: Two wire-to-wire processions in opposite directions: Stuart Neumann finally converts a decade of climbing (6th, 5th, 3rd, 2nd) into a first Trophy, while Alex Baker, the reigning Spoon holder, is bottom of the pile from the very first hole and rewrites two course-worsts on the way — and Gregg Williams, unable to defend the Trophy, quietly builds a 16-shot Green Jacket instead.
tone: house — faithful, tongue-in-cheek, Ronay/Peck register: affectionate ribbing anchored to real numbers, no zaniness
opening_hook: Open on the R4 scorecards at Estoril — Portugal's oldest and gentlest course handing out a new record 80 (Mullin, cr01) and a new course-worst 107 (Alex Baker, cr02) on the same afternoon, 27 shots apart — then step back to show that the whole tournament had been running in those two directions since R1 H1.
foreshadow: Neumann arrives with no Trophy, no Jacket, two Wooden Spoons, and a career ladder that reads 6th (TEG 9), 5th (TEG 10), 3rd (TEG 12), 2nd (TEG 15) — one rung left
Alex Baker arrives as reigning Spoon holder from TEG 15 with two prior Spoons, and opens the tournament with a 9 at the 1st at Oitavos Dunes (b07)
Gregg Williams arrives as defending Trophy champion with only one Jacket to his name — the defence goes one way, the gross goes another
Estoril, the shortest and least fearsome course of the four, is trailed early as the place where the tournament's widest numbers would be written

competitions.name: Trophy (Stableford)
competitions.winner_or_loser: Stuart Neumann — winner, 156 pts, by 13 from Gregg Williams
competitions.how: Neumann led after every round: 39 pts at Oitavos Dunes for a 5-point cushion, 35 at Troia (lead 7), 39 at Penha Longa (lead 12) and a tournament-best 43 at Estoril (lead 13). The only lead changes came at R1 H4 and H5, while the field was still bunched — routine, and never repeated. The R3 39 at Penha Longa, on the hardest layout of the four, was the round that turned a lead into an unbridgeable gap; the R4 43 was decoration, and survived his own 9 at Estoril's SI 1 8th (b05, b22).

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.winner_or_loser: Gregg Williams — winner, +66, by 16 from David Mullin
competitions.how: Williams led the gross from R1 to R4 without interruption: a personal-best 89 at Oitavos Dunes (lead 3), 94 at Troia (lead 4), then the decisive move — 87 at Penha Longa while Jon Baker went round in 97 and Mullin in 98, blowing the margin out from 4 to 14. Mullin's record 80 at Estoril in R4 (cr01) was two rounds too late; Williams matched him with an 80 of his own and won by 16.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.how: Bottom of the pile from R1 H1 and never above 5th at any round's end. Oitavos Dunes brought a 113 — a new course-worst across 13 visits (cr03) — built from a 9 at the 1st (b07), a 9 at the 7th (b23), a 9 at the 11th (b08) and a 10 at the 17th (b04). R1's bottom spot briefly changed hands with Mullin five times before H15; the last word came at Troia, R2 H13, where a triple bogey (b43) dropped him to outright last for good. R3 and R4 were confirmation: 33 and 33, a 107 at Estoril (cr02, another course-worst) and an 11 at the 12th (b03), his worst hole against par on record.

rounds.chosen_headline: The Thirteenth at Troia Settles the Spoon Before Anyone Notices
rounds.angle: A brand-new TEG course, and the day's only lasting decision is at the bottom: Alex Baker's triple at H13 (b43) drops him to outright last for the remaining 42 holes, while Neumann's 11 points in three holes (b19) and 35 total push the Trophy lead to 7 despite a triple at the 13th of his own (b34) and an 8 at the 16th (b11).

rounds.chosen_headline: Penha Longa Bites: Williams 87, Everyone Else Backwards
rounds.angle: The mountain course decides the Green Jacket — Williams's 87 against Jon Baker's 97 and Mullin's 98 turns a 4-shot lead into 14 — while Neumann's 39 pts, blemishes and all, stretches the Trophy lead to 12; Jon Baker's 10 at the 12th (b09) comes at the easiest hole on the card, SI 17.

headline_candidates: Twenty-Seven Shots Apart: Estoril's Record and Its Rock Bottom
Mullin Shoots 80 Two Days Too Late
Neumann Signs for 43 and Finally Gets His Hands on Something
rounds.chosen_headline: Twenty-Seven Shots Apart: Estoril's Record and Its Rock Bottom
rounds.angle: Portugal's oldest, shortest course produces both extremes in one afternoon — Mullin's record 80 (cr01), matched by Williams for a PB, and Alex Baker's 107 course-worst (cr02) with an 11 at the 12th (b03) — while Neumann shrugs off a 9 at SI 1 (b05) to post 43 and win the Trophy by 13.

players.arc: No Trophy, no Jacket and two Wooden Spoons to his name, with finishes reading 6th, 5th, 3rd, 2nd across his last four TEGs — he leads this one from the first evening to the last, closes with a tournament-best 43, and takes the ladder's final rung by 13.

Defending Trophy champion who never gets near defending it, and instead turns a PB 89 at Oitavos and an 87 at Penha Longa into a second Green Jacket by 16, finishing second on Stableford as a consolation.
Reigning Spoon holder who is last from R1 H1 to the final putt, collecting two course-worsts (cr03, cr02), an 11 at Estoril's 12th and a back-to-back Wooden Spoon on 127 pts.

Nine-time Jacket winner who spends three rounds nowhere — 13 shots worse than his TEG 15 self at Penha Longa — then rips the Estoril course record apart with an 80 (cr01), 14 better than his last visit, and still loses the Jacket by 16.
Personal bests at Oitavos (92) and Estoril (93) bracket a Penha Longa 97 — twelve worse than last time — in which a 10 at the 12th (b09) and an 8 at the 13th quietly hand Williams the Jacket.

venue_notes: TEG's 5th visit to the Lisbon Coast, and four very different courses: Oitavos Dunes (Arthur Hills links, 3rd TEG round here) opens with Atlantic dunes and hands out a course-worst; Troia (Robert Trent Jones Sr., a new course for TEG — everyone's first visit, so no history to lean on, just RTJ strategy) hosts the quiet moment the Spoon is settled; Penha Longa's Sintra mountainside (3rd TEG round here) is where the Jacket is decided by attrition; Estoril (2nd TEG round here, Portugal's first club, Mackenzie Ross parkland, the shortest and gentlest of the four) improbably produces both the record 80 and the 107.
course_history_notes: Mullin's new Estoril PB in R4: 80 gross, 14 better than his TEG 15 visit — and a new course record (cr01), beating 86 set across 6 prior visits
Williams also went round Estoril in 80 for his own PB there (prior best 86, TEG 15), and set a new Oitavos Dunes PB of 89 in R1 (prior best 91)
Neumann was 14 shots better than his last visit to Estoril — 92 against 106 in TEG 15 — the improvement that turned a 43-point round into a Trophy
Alex Baker was 10 worse than his last visit at Oitavos Dunes (113 v 103) and 8 worse at Estoril (107 v 99): two course-worsts, cr03 and cr02
decisive_moments: R3 at Penha Longa — Neumann's 39 pts on the hardest layout of the four stretched a 7-point Trophy lead to 12 and made the last round a formality; the win was sealed with a 43 at Estoril for 156 pts, by 13
R3 at Penha Longa — Williams's 87 against Jon Baker's 97 and Mullin's 98 turned a 4-shot Green Jacket lead into 14, and Mullin's record 80 in R4 (cr01) could only trim it to 16
R2 H13 at Troia — Alex Baker's triple bogey (b43) dropped him to outright bottom of the Spoon race, and he stayed there for the remaining 42 holes

vehicle_fit_response.note: Taken up — Alex Baker's seven blow-ups plus two course-worsts are a genuine inventory, and they form the descending half of the dual narrative against Neumann's career climb; origin scored well too but hero_arc better captures the 6-5-3-2-1 ladder, and origin was last TEG's frame.
